subject: Security readiness: evidence checklist, breach-notif path, and next steps
messages:
-----Original Message-----
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Wright <anna.wright@bluestonehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Security readiness: evidence checklist, breach-notif path, and next steps

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and clear next steps so your security and procurement teams have what they need.

Recap from call:
- BlueStone is evaluating Redwood for patient-facing summarization and triage workflows (PHI in scope).
- Key asks: SOC 2 status, HIPAA attestation, breach notification timelines (contractual 72-hour notice), and BCP/DR evidence for audit.
- You asked for a starter packet we can hand to Security/Procurement that calls out timelines and sample artifacts.

What I’m attaching here: a short IR/BCP playbook extract and our SOC 2 quick-summary (see attachments). Those are design-level artifacts to start — we can follow with the full evidence set under an NDA or through your secured portal.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share the initial packet (attached) with a one-page mapping to HIPAA controls we discussed.
2) Please complete the attached security questionnaire (we added a tab for PHI-specific controls) and return by EOD Friday 5/22 if possible.
3) We propose a short follow-up with our IR lead (Rishi) and your security lead to walk the breach-notification flow and confirm SLA language — would Thu 5/21 11:00 PT work?

Breach-notification summary (from platform side):
- Detection and initial triage: within hours of alert.
- Internal escalation and containment: typically within 4–8 hours of detection depending on severity.
- Customer notification window: we contractually commit to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming a notifiable breach; for critical PII/PHI exposures we accelerate communication and will provide a preliminary summary within 24–48 hours while the full root cause analysis is underway.

Please let me know if the timeline above matches your expectations. If you prefer, we can route the complete evidence package via your secure SFTP/ShareFile link — send the transfer details and we’ll push the files.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs:
- rdw-ir-playbook.pdf (excerpt: IR runbook, notification steps, contact matrix)
- soc2-quick-summary-2025.pdf (scope, auditor, coverage)

-----Reply-----
From: Anna Wright <anna.wright@bluestonehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@bluestonehealth.com, DPO Team <dpo@bluestonehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security readiness: evidence checklist, breach-notif path, and next steps

Thanks, Irene — packet received and looks helpful. Quick clarifying items from our InfoSec team: 
1) SOC 2: we need to confirm whether Redwood is Type II and the date range for the last audit.
2) For HIPAA/BAA: we require the BAA to call out the 72-hour notification commitment and a retention clause for audit logs for 7 years.
3) Can you confirm whether your IR timeline above includes time to perform forensic validation before notification? Our legal team expects notification within 72 hours of confirmation, not of initial detection.

We can do Thu 5/21 11:00 PT for a short sync — I’ll bring our security lead, Karla, and DPO Dawn. I’ll also return the questionnaire by Friday if possible.

—Anna
Anna Wright
Head of Security Operations
BlueStone Health

-----Forwarded Message (internal)-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security readiness: evidence checklist, breach-notif path, and next steps

Irene — thanks for pulling this together. A few internal notes before the call: 
- SOC 2 status: Redwood completed a Type II in 2024 for the Hosted API scope; Dedicated & Private deployment packages have a scoped control matrix and are supported by system descriptions and evidence. We should be explicit about which deployment modalities BlueStone plans to use (they mentioned private VPC for PHI).
- Forensics vs confirmation: our standard process is to perform rapid containment and a targeted forensic validation; legal/ops define whether an event meets the threshold for a notifiable breach. We should articulate that notification timing is tied to confirmation, and we will provide an initial notification within 24–48 hours when we have high-confidence indicators plus an update within 72 hours with more details.
- Evidence packaging: recommend offering an NDA and SFTP for PHI-scoped evidence to avoid sending full artifacts over email.

Irene, Monica — I’ll lead the call on Thursday to walk the IR flow and BCP extracts. Monica, can you bring the redlines we typically share for BAA language (72-hour notification clause and log-retention language)?

-Rishi

-----Reply All (internal -> external)-----
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Wright <anna.wright@bluestonehealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@bluestonehealth.com, DPO Team <dpo@bluestonehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security readiness: evidence checklist, breach-notif path, and next steps

Hi Anna — good to meet you on the call earlier. Per request, I’m attaching the security questionnaire (filled with initial answers) and a proposed BAA clause snippet we typically include for PHI customers. Highlights: 
- SOC 2: Type II completed for Hosted API (audit: Nov 2024 coverage). For Private deployments we provide system descriptions and control evidence in-scope by deployment; we will note the controls that map to HIPAA.
- Notification wording: proposed clause — "Provider will notify Customer of confirmed unauthorized disclosures of Customer Data that constitute a notifiable breach within 72 hours of confirmation; Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a preliminary notification within 48 hours when feasible and will include a summary of impacted data classes and immediate containment steps."
- Log retention: we can commit to seven years for audit logs where technically feasible; for ephemeral runtime caches we’ll explain retention limits and available alternatives (archival endpoints, SIEM integration).

Attachments (stubs):
- bluestone-security-questionnaire-v1.xlsx (tab: answers + PHI controls)
- proposed-baa-snippet.txt

Next steps (action items):
- Anna/Dawn/Karla: review the questionnaire answers and proposed BAA snippet and flag any required redlines by 5/28.
- Irene/Rishi/Monica: prepare a secure evidence package and NDA template; we’ll offer SFTP or your portal upload by 5/26 pending NDA.

If you want, I can also send a short export of sample IR timelines (anonymized) that show detection -> containment -> notification in practice.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Security Manager, Product Security Ops
Redwood Inference
